outcome: Preda Mihăilescu (preprint, 22 Sep 2025) proved via a cyclotomic argument (Stickelberger ideal, Jacobi sums) that the equation (x^p+y^p)/(x+y) = p^e z^q has no solutions in coprime integers for p>3, q distinct odd primes, and states as a direct corollary that the classical Fermat-Catalan equation x^p+y^p=z^q has no solutions for that signature family — settling one infinite family of exponent triples (p,p,q), p>3, q an odd prime ≠ p. The general finiteness conjecture remains open. Separately, a December 2024 survey (Ratcliffe–Grechuk, published in Expositiones Mathematicae 2025) reports that Sikora's computational search of the classical Fermat-Catalan equation was extended to cover all coprime solutions with z^r ≤ 2^100, still finding only the same ten known solutions; this narrows where an eleventh solution could hide but does not itself settle the existence question (per the rule that a record/search-bound extension does not count as progress on a 'finitely many / are there more' question unless the record itself is the object of the bullet).
summary: The triage's `none` verdict correctly identified that no proof or disproof of the general finiteness conjecture, and no new qualifying solution, has appeared since 26 January 2024 — the conjecture as a whole is exactly as open as it was. But the triage mischaracterized Mihăilescu's September 2025 paper as 'unrelated cyclotomic work... on a different variant equation,' which I disagree with (triage_disagreement). Reading the paper directly (arXiv:2509.18275, HTML version), its Theorem 1 explicitly states two things in sequence: (1) the 'strong' quotient equation (x^p+y^p)/(x+y)=p^e z^q has no coprime solutions for p>3, q distinct odd primes, and (2) 'In particular, the Fermat-Catalan equation ... has no solutions with distinct odd primes p,q and p>3.' That second clause is a direct statement about the classical equation a^m+b^n=c^k with (m,n,k)=(p,p,q) — a restriction of the problem to a specific infinite family of exponent triples, which is a case of the stated problem under §3.1, not a variant with changed hypotheses (the object equation, coprimality condition, and exponent inequality 1/p+1/p+1/q<1 for p>3,q≥5 are all exactly the Fermat-Catalan setup). This is exactly the shape of result the deep-dive rules count as `partial`: a slice of the exponent-triple space is now provably solution-free, narrowing (removing territory from) the general conjecture, even though the conjecture as a whole stays open. Separately, the Ratcliffe–Grechuk survey (Dec 2024, revised Apr 2025, published in Expositiones Mathematicae) extended Sikora's exhaustive computational search to z^r ≤ 2^100, confirming no solutions beyond the known ten in that range and naming (2,5,7) and (3,5,7) as the smallest open signatures — this is real computational work but, per §3.1's rule for existence/infinitude questions, a larger search bound narrows where a counterexample could hide without answering whether one exists, so on its own it would not move status past `open`; it is reported here as context for the `partial` finding, not as an independent basis for it. No AI or machine-learning system appears in either paper: Mihăilescu's acknowledgements name only human colleagues and students, and both papers' computational work (ALICE HPC / University at Buffalo cluster) is exhaustive integer search, not a learned model. I also checked Sikora's October 2024 paper (arXiv:2410.21552), which proposes conjectural product-generalizations of Fermat-Catalan/Tijdeman-Zagier rather than proving anything about the classical equation itself — that one is correctly a variant, not a case, and contributes nothing to status. Anthropic's 2026 formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean is an unrelated problem (fixed equal exponents m=n=k, no coprime a,b,c<1 inequality structure) and does not bear on this record.
competing_reading: One could argue the Mihăilescu result is 'about' the strong/quotient equation and only mentions the classical Fermat-Catalan equation as an aside ('in particular'), so it might be read as a related/variant result rather than a case of the stated problem, especially since the paper's title and main technical machinery target the quotient form. Under that reading the correct status would remain `open` with `no_change_found` true (aside from the stale search-bound extension). I do not adopt this reading because Theorem 1 states the classical-equation non-existence result explicitly and unconditionally for that exponent family, and the deep-dive rule for a 'case' is about restricting the stated question, which is exactly what fixing (m,n,k)=(p,p,q), p>3 does — the route to the result (via the quotient identity) does not change what the result claims about the original equation.
what_would_settle_it: Expert digestion or journal acceptance of Mihăilescu's preprint would move this specific case from a preprint-only partial toward a firmly established partial result (it does not need 'resolved' since it only ever settles a case, not the whole conjecture). Any future paper explicitly extending or contradicting the (p,p,q) family result, or a full proof/disproof of the general finiteness conjecture, would supersede this record.

corrections.why: other: The status is kept. The (p,p,q) family is a genuine restriction of the bullet's equation (a case, not a variant), so it counts. But the claim is unreviewed and very strong for the field, so it is credible only with doubt, and the status is fragile if the preprint fails.

events.what: Mihăilescu's preprint claims that (x^p+y^p)/(x+y) = p^e z^q has no coprime solutions for distinct odd primes p>3, q, and hence that x^p+y^p=z^q has none for that signature family
events.credibility_reason: The author is an established cyclotomic specialist (the record names him as the Catalan prover), but the claim settles a whole infinite two-parameter family of signatures (p,p,q), far beyond known modular-method results. It is a single-author preprint, and the record shows no expert uptake yet.

events.what: A survey reports Sikora's search extended to z^r ≤ 2^100, finding only the ten known solutions
Sikora proposes conjectural product generalisations of Fermat–Catalan

judgement.doubts: The codes stand. The partial result rests on an unreviewed single-author preprint whose claim is unusually strong for this problem. If it is rebutted, the status should revert to open. The 2^100 search counts only as instances.
